title: The Canon of Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The canon of Scripture is the collection of writings God has given as His authoritative Word. The church does not create Scripture’s authority; it receives and recognizes the Scriptures God has given.
summary: The canon of Scripture is the collection of writings God has given as His authoritative Word. The church does not create Scripture’s authority; it receives and recognizes the Scriptures God has given.
christFocus: Jesus received the Scriptures as the Word of God and showed that the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms pointed to Him. The canon is not a random religious library; it is God’s written witness to His redemptive purpose fulfilled in Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The canon of Scripture teaches that God has given His people a defined and authoritative Word. God did not leave His church with endless uncertainty about what carries divine authority. He spoke, preserved His Word, and led His people to receive what He gave.

The church does not make a writing Scripture by voting on it or placing authority into it. Scripture carries authority because it comes from God. The people of God recognize the voice and authority of God in the writings He has given.

The Old Testament Scriptures were received by Jesus and His apostles as God’s Word. The New Testament writings bear apostolic authority and testify to the fulfillment of God’s saving work in Christ. Together, the Scriptures reveal creation, fall, promise, covenant, redemption, fulfillment, and eternal hope.

The canon also warns believers not to add to or take away from God’s Word. Faithfulness requires receiving what God has spoken without trying to improve, reduce, replace, or revise His authority.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often want a faith they can adjust. Some want to remove hard truths. Others want to add new revelations, private authorities, or teachings that compete with Scripture. The canon protects the church from being ruled by spiritual confusion, human control, or endless claims of authority.

This doctrine gives believers a stable foundation. God’s people are not left chasing every voice that claims to speak for Him. The church is called to hear, trust, teach, and obey the Scriptures God has given.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Treasure the completed Scriptures as God’s sufficient written Word. Do not build your faith on secret knowledge, spiritual trends, personal revelations, or teachings that stand above the Bible. Let the whole counsel of God shape your doctrine, worship, obedience, and hope in Christ.
